versions.text: When the river that drowned her town in 1965 rises again, a retired schoolteacher opens the flood diary she has kept secret for sixty years.
A retired schoolteacher opens the flood diary she has kept for sixty years as the river rises again.

Riverside has flooded three times in living memory. Ruth Hammond kept a diary through the first, Leon Pryor fought the second from the levee board, and Daniel Okafor is still finding his grandmother's photographs of the third. As engineers argue over whether the new levee will hold, The River Keeps follows the people who remember what the water took, and asks what a town owes the ones who stayed.

Riverside has flooded three times in living memory. A schoolteacher kept a diary through the first, a levee board member fought the second, and a grandson is still finding photographs of the third. As engineers argue over the new levee, The River Keeps follows the people who remember what the water took, and asks what a town owes the ones who stayed behind when the water came.

We will screen The River Keeps in the six river towns where it was filmed, with county emergency managers and historical societies, and give every library in the county a copy with a discussion guide. The film's oral histories, with consent, will go to the county historical society's flood archive, so the people who remember are heard by the people who plan.

Ana Reyes is a producer whose documentaries follow small towns through big changes. She runs Lowwater Films and has produced work for public television and regional festivals. The River Keeps is her first feature as producer.
